title: THE FINAL STRETCH TO THE JORDAN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They left Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah. They left Zalmonah and camped at Punon. They left Punon and camped at Oboth. They left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, on the border of Moab. They left Iye Abarim and camped at Dibon Gad. They left Dibon Gad and camped at Almon Diblathaim. They left Almon Diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, near Nebo. They left the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho. Here on the plains of Moab they camped along the Jordan from Beth Jeshimoth to Abel Shittim. - Num 33:41-49 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At last the journey reaches its final campsite: "the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho." After forty years, after all the deserts and detours, Israel stands at the very edge of the Promised Land. Just across the river lies everything God had sworn to give them. The long journey is nearly complete; they are one river away from home.

What a moment this must have been. From these plains they could look across the Jordan and see the land of promise. The God who had led them out of Egypt, through the sea, across the wilderness, and past every enemy had brought them right to the threshold. He had been faithful to every word.

There is deep encouragement here for weary travellers. God finishes what He starts. He does not lead His people halfway and then abandon them. The One who began the journey out of Egypt brought them to the banks of the Jordan, and He would carry them across. As Paul says, He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion (Phil 1:6).

Wherever you are on your journey, take heart: God is bringing you home. There may be a Jordan still to cross, a final stretch that requires faith. But the God who has led you this far will not fail you at the border. Every promise finds its yes in Christ (2 Cor 1:20), and He will bring His people safely into their eternal inheritance. The plains of Moab remind us: the destination is in sight, because God is faithful.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you see how far God has already brought you on your journey?
2. What "Jordan" of faith might God be calling you to cross next?
3. How does God's track record of faithfulness strengthen your hope for the future?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, You have led me this far and I trust You to carry me the rest of the way. Give me courage to cross whatever Jordan lies ahead, resting in Your promise to complete the good work You began in me. Amen.
